products.name: Manfrotto PIXI Mini Tripod (MTPIXI-B)
products.query: Manfrotto PIXI mini tripod black MTPIXI-B
products.summary: A fixed-height tabletop tripod with a push-button ball head and legs that fold into a grip. Digital Camera World leads its mini tripod guide with it and says it works for video conferencing at home.
products.renterNote: Anyone putting a light webcam, phone (with a clamp) or compact camera on a desk for calls. Key caveat: height is fixed at about 13.5 cm and the head tilts up only about 35 degrees, so it sits low and you may need books or a riser for eye level.
pros: Solid, simple build with a ball head reviewers say works well
Rated for about 1 kg, plenty for a webcam or phone
Legs fold into a grip, so it packs small and doubles as a handle
cons: No height adjustment, so the lens sits low on a desk
Ball head is stiff, tilts upward only about 35 degrees and shoots landscape only; phones need a separate clamp

specs.Head: Ball head with push-button release, about 35 degrees upward tilt
specs.Plate: 1/4 in screw mount; phone clamp sold separately

products.scoreNote: Compact, solid and trustworthy for light gear, but fixed at about 13.5 cm with limited tilt, so it scores low on working height.

praise: Solid, sturdy support for its size
Easy to adjust with a squeeze of the release, and usable as a hand grip with legs folded
complaints: Fixed 13 cm height makes it hard to raise the lens
Spring-loaded ball head release is stiff and tilt is limited to roughly 35 degrees

Cold shoe mount for a microphone or small light

products.name: SmallRig Mini Tabletop Tripod with Panoramic Ball Head (BUT2664)
products.query: SmallRig mini tabletop tripod Arca-type QR plate BUT2664
products.badge: Best for a mirrorless camera on the desk
products.summary: An all-aluminum tabletop tripod with a 360-degree panoramic ball head and an Arca-type quick-release plate. Lynn Barsigian Photography names it best overall tabletop tripod, and its owner write-up says it is a go-to desk tripod that held a Sony A7IV with a 24-70mm lens without creep.
products.renterNote: Remote workers and streamers who put a mirrorless or compact camera (or a webcam on a 1/4 in mount) on the desk for calls. Key caveat: it is only about 9 in tall with the head, so the lens sits low and you may need a riser for eye level, and at about 410 g it is not the lightest option.
pros: All-aluminum build that an owner write-up describes as having no flex or creaking
Ball head rated for about 2 kg (4.4 lb), enough for a mirrorless body and a short lens
Arca-type quick-release plate and a panoramic head with independent pan
cons: Only about 9 in tall, so the lens sits low on a desk without a riser
About 410 g, heavier than the other minis here; one reviewer calls the plate size non-standard, and the legs need a hex tool to hold an intermediate angle

specs.Weight: About 14.4 oz (410 g) (Full Compass; Lynn Barsigian Photography)
specs.Max load: 4.4 lb (2 kg) at the ball head; some listings say the legs alone hold more
specs.Leg lock: None; leg angle is set with a hex tool for intermediate positions per an Adorama reviewer
specs.Head: 360-degree panoramic ball head, -90/+45 degree front tilt, +/-50 degree lateral tilt
specs.Plate: Arca-type quick-release plate with 1/4 in-20 screw

products.scoreNote: Rigid aluminum legs and a head that held a mirrorless kit make it the steadiest here, but it is about 410 g and only about 9 in tall, so working height is low.

Head held steady with no creep under a Sony A7IV and 24-70mm lens (owner write-up)
complaints: Heavier than advertised at about 410 g

Arca plate size called non-standard by one reviewer
